name: Doremy's IQ
description: Doremy is asked to test $$$n$$$ contests. Contest $$$i$$$ can only be tested on day $$$i$$$. The difficulty of contest $$$i$$$ is $$$a_i$$$. Initially, Doremy's IQ is $$$q$$$. On day $$$i$$$ Doremy will choose whether to test contest $$$i$$$ or not. She can only test a contest if her current IQ is strictly greater than $$$0$$$. If Doremy chooses to test contest $$$i$$$ on day $$$i$$$, the following happens: if $$$a_i \gt q$$$, Doremy will feel she is not wise enough, so $$$q$$$ decreases by $$$1$$$; otherwise, nothing changes. If she chooses not to test a contest, nothing changes. Doremy wants to test as many contests as possible. Please give Doremy a solution.
input_specification: The input consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le q \le 10^9$$$) — the number of contests and Doremy's IQ in the beginning. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\cdots,a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the difficulty of each contest. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, you need to output a binary string $$$s$$$, where $$$s_i=1$$$ if Doremy should choose to test contest $$$i$$$, and $$$s_i=0$$$ otherwise. The number of ones in the string should be maximum possible, and she should never test a contest when her IQ is zero or less. If there are multiple solutions, you may output any.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1707A — Doremy's IQ [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
